subject: Monthly dashboard review: latency & cost anomalies + action playbook
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Cc: Claire Zhang <claire@acme-cloud.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Monthly dashboard review: latency & cost anomalies + action playbook

Team —

I pulled the July dashboards and flagged two items we need to resolve before QBR prep next week:

1) P50/P95 tail spike on hosted-inference in us-west between 11:00–15:00 PDT on 7/14 and 7/21 (average P95 up ~35% vs. baseline).
2) Token cost creep driven by an unexpected increase in small-batch burst traffic for embedding requests (estimated +18% unit cost).

I've attached the PDF summary and the tokenized uptime logs. High level ask: can each owner own an investigation + short remediation proposal by EOD Mon (8/2)? Suggested owners:
- Latency investigation & mitigation: Laura + Marcus
- Cost root cause & quick wins (batching/quantization): Evelyn + Jonas

Claire — including Acme since some traces show increased traffic from their integration during the window. If you can confirm whether they rolled out a client-side change on 7/14 / 7/21, that would help.

Deliverable format: 1-slide summary + 3 bullet remediation options, rough impact estimates, and one immediate action we can ship in <72 hours.

Thanks,
Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Director, Commercial Strategy
Redwood Inference

Attachments: 2026-07-monthly-dashboard.pdf (summary), uptime-tokenized-logs-2026-07.csv (sampling)
From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Claire Zhang <claire@acme-cloud.com>
Date: Wed, 29 Jul 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Monthly dashboard review: latency & cost anomalies + action playbook

Rishi — thanks for the heads up. Quick update from infra side: we already have traces for both dates and a preliminary hypothesis: the P95 spikes align with two separate autoscaler thrash events for the hosted-inference pool triggered by a surge of short-lived VCPU-bound fanout requests. Preliminary notes:

- Autoscaler oscillation around 200–230 GPUs during those windows.
- Elevated queue latency at the routing layer when models with long KV caches were routed to freshly spun instances.

Immediate 72-hour action (what we can ship quickly):
- Tighten autoscaler stabilization window from 30s -> 90s for hosted-inference pools (low risk, config change).
- Prioritize warm routing for model variants with kv-cache > 4GB for hot paths.

Will put together the slide with traces and estimated latency uplift if we apply both mitigations. Marcus will help with the kernel/serving timeline.

Laura
VP, Serving Infrastructure

Subject: Re: Monthly dashboard review: latency & cost anomalies + action playbook

Adding implementation detail: after Laura's investigation we'll propose a two-track approach for the latency side:

Track A (fast): config changes — increase autoscaler stabilization to 90s, enforce warm-routing for large-kv models, and add a short backoff for routing retries. Expected improvement: reduce the P95 spike by ~20–30% within 24–72 hours; negligible cost impact.

Track B (medium): kernel/serving optimization — prefetch KV index on spin-up and optimize kernel selection for long-history contexts. Expected improvement: further 10–15% on P95, requires a 2-week engineering sprint.

I'll produce a one-slide engineering impact estimate and include a risk section.

Marcus
Principal Engineer, Model Serving

Date: Fri, 31 Jul 2026 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Monthly dashboard review: latency & cost anomalies + action playbook

Team — quick cost-side findings: the embedding traffic increase is concentrated in small batch sizes (1–4) from a handful of API keys tied to Acme integrations. Estimated incremental token cost impact: +$12k for July (projected monthly run rate if unchanged).

Quick wins (72-hour):
- Apply server-side batching threshold: coalesce small embedding requests into a short 25ms batching window for non-interactive routes (low risk; reversible).
- Push a recommended client change to use batch submission for bulk embedding jobs; include a small SDK example.

Longer items: quantization profile adjustment for embedding models (2–3 week runway) and a caching TTL for repeated client prefixes. I'll draft a single slide with numbers and expected dollar savings per option.

Evelyn
Head of Platform Economics

Rishi / Evelyn — thanks for looping us in. I confirmed our client team rolled out a patched worker on 7/14 that changed our batching behavior (we inadvertently started sending many 1-2 request bursts instead of batching). We're rolling a fix this week; procurement looped in to check contract usage terms.

We appreciate the suggested server-side batching and will coordinate on SDK examples. Let me know if you want us to throttle the integration while you apply infra mitigations.

Claire

- Laura & Marcus: finalize single-slide mitigation proposal for Track A (config) and Track B (serving optimizations). Deliverable: slide + expected P95 impact + rollout plan. (Due: Tue 8/3 EOD)
- Evelyn & Jonas: finalize cost play with dollarized savings for server-side batching + SDK note. Deliverable: slide + savings estimate + quick rollout steps. (Due: Tue 8/3 EOD)
- Claire / Acme: test fix in staging and confirm whether temporary throttling is needed.

I'll assemble the slides into the QBR pack on Wed morning and share a draft by 8/4 09:00 PDT. If anyone needs additional logs or queries, point to the Drive folder I dropped in related_links.
